title: Delete rings, including ring_candidates rings, and load ring_candidates rings with anchors
description:
User review 2026-10-03 of the CRAW-30 ring tool (authored and supporting anchors, drafts); builds on CRAW-30's baseline. The user's 17 saved fertility rings (fixtures/fertility_rings.dsl: ring_candidates plus spline_ring ring_05 to ring_17) must survive the change and reload element-exact.

Delete rings, including the recommended ones, and give recommended rings anchors from the start.
1. Delete a ring: with a ring open as the draft and no anchor selected, Delete/Backspace removes the whole ring. The next Ctrl+S removes its statement from the working .dsl (RingDslWriter gains remove-by-id next to replaceSpline). Undoable once the undo/redo stack ticket lands.
2. The rings ring_candidates produces are deletable the same way, and the deletion persists through save and reload: either convert the candidates to spline_ring statements or add an exclusion argument to ring_candidates; pick one and record why.
3. A ring_candidates ring is an editable anchored ring from the moment it loads (authored anchors shown when it is selected), not a bare edge line that only gets anchors once clicked.

Rework 2026-10-03 (user review, before landing): drop the exclude= representation. A ring_candidates line produces all its rings on every load, so excluding by rank grows forever and silently points at a different ring when the mesh, the parameters or the detector shift. The user does not like the candidate rings' placement and expects to delete them on new models, so deleting them must be a real delete.

Freeze on first edit. The first time the user deletes or edits any ring that comes from a ring_candidates statement, the tool replaces that statement in the working .dsl with one statement per surviving candidate ring, each carrying that ring's exact edge loop (an ordered vertex loop, not a refitted spline, so every frozen ring reloads element-exact: same fingerprint as the candidate it came from). The ring_candidates statement is then gone; the frozen rings keep their labels and their order in the chain. From then on a delete removes that ring's line, as it already does for spline_ring. Deleting every frozen ring leaves no ring statement behind. Use loop_through_points with every vertex pinned if it reproduces the loop exactly; otherwise add a minimal exact-loop statement (for example edge_loop(points=...)). Remove the exclude input from RingCandidatesNode and its tests. Undo (CRAW-34's history) must restore the pre-freeze state in memory, and a save after that undo must write the ring_candidates statement back.
definition-of-done:
1. Deleting a spline_ring and a ring_candidates ring, saving and reloading leaves both gone and every other ring element-exact (fingerprints unchanged). 2. ring_candidates rings show authored anchors when selected, without a click to convert them. 3. The chosen persistence for deleted candidates is recorded on the ticket. 4. Build checkstyle-green.

Rework (2026-10-03):
F1. On a copy of fertility_rings.dsl, deleting ring_03 and saving replaces the ring_candidates line with exact-loop statements for ring_00, ring_01, ring_02 and ring_04; the file has no exclude= anywhere; reloading gives the 17 remaining rings with fingerprints identical to before.
F2. Deleting a frozen ring afterwards removes its line; deleting all five candidate rings leaves neither a ring_candidates line nor any frozen statement.
F3. Editing (not deleting) a candidate ring freezes the others too, and the edited one is saved as a spline_ring.
F4. Ctrl+Z after a freeze restores the candidate state, and saving then writes the ring_candidates line back.
testing-plan: 1. Unit test: RingDslWriter remove-by-id round trip. 2. Unit test: delete, save and reload on a fixture keeps the other fingerprints. 3. F5 on fertility with screenshots before and after deleting each kind.
changes-made: Persistence (DoD 3): a deleted spline_ring statement is removed from the .dsl (RingDslWriter.remove rewires its reader, e.g. ring_06 now reads rings.geometry); a deleted ring_candidates ring is recorded as ring_candidates(..., exclude="ring_03"). Chosen over converting candidates to spline_ring statements because converting replaces each proposal's exact FlipOut edge loop with a fitted spline (ring_03: 41 edges exact vs 40 fitted), so the surviving candidates would not reload element-exact; the exclusion keeps the other candidates' labels and fingerprints and the extractor untouched. An edited candidate is saved as a new spline_ring plus an exclusion of its label.

Load: every graph ring is a confirmed ring with authored anchors from the first frame (RingTool.adoptGraphRings): spline_ring statements retrace their own points+normal (all 13 fingerprints equal the graph's), ring_candidates rings get anchors fitted to their loop and keep drawing the exact loop until edited. 18 rings in 25 ms on fertility.

Delete: Delete/Backspace with a ring open as the draft and no anchor selected deletes the ring (RingTool.deleteDraftRing/deleteRing), recorded in the CRAW-34 history as 'ring deleted' (Ctrl+Z restores it, Ctrl+Y re-deletes). Ctrl+S removes or excludes it; a save also removes a statement whose ring was undone after an earlier save, so the .dsl matches memory.

Verification on a copy (tmp/fertility_rings_craw35.dsl, fixture untouched): load shows 18 rings, fingerprints recorded; deleted ring_05 (spline) and ring_03 (candidate), saved, relaunched: 16 rings, ring_03 and ring_05 gone, the other 16 fingerprints identical. Confirm+save+undo+save restores the file byte-identical. Edit of candidate ring_00 saved as ring_18 with exclude="ring_03, ring_00". Screenshots tmp/craw35-02..10*.png. mvn -q compile green (checkstyle), mvn test 344/344 incl. RingDslWriterTest (remove/exclude round trips) and RingDeletionTest (delete, save, reload keeps the other fingerprints on the procedural Y).

Rework 2026-10-03 (freeze on first edit): exclude= is gone (RingCandidatesNode/RingCandidates back to master, catalog entry removed). A save that finds any proposed ring deleted or edited rewrites the ring_candidates line as one statement per live proposed ring, bound to its label, in rank order: loop_through_points(points=<every loop vertex in walking order>, tighten=true, pin=true, label=ring_NN) for an unedited ring, spline_ring for an edited one; readers are rewired (RingDslWriter.replaceBlock/replace/insertAfter). Exact-loop evidence: every vertex pinned leaves FlipOut nothing to move, and on fertility the 4 frozen rings reload with fingerprints identical to the candidates (F1); RingDeletionTest checks the same on the procedural Y in array form. loop_through_points and spline_ring now convert an array mesh to the half-edge form, as ring_candidates already did, so a frozen ring or spline ring that reads load_mesh directly runs on the same mesh (before this change loop_through_points threw 'mesh is not manifold' on fertility_in_tri.off). The tool remembers the ring_candidates line, and a save while every proposed ring is live and unedited writes it back. Verified on tmp copies of the 18-ring fixture through the automation routes: F1 delete ring_03 + Ctrl+S froze ring_00/01/02/04, no exclude=, relaunch gave 17 rings with fingerprints identical; F2 deleting frozen ring_02 in a fresh session removed its line, deleting ring_00/01/04 left no loop_through_points or ring_candidates line (ring_05 reads carrier.geometry) and the 13 spline rings reloaded identical; deleting all five in one session wrote the same file; F3 adding an anchor to ring_01 froze the others and saved ring_01 = spline_ring in place, reload identical to the saving session; F4 Ctrl+Z after a freeze save then Ctrl+S restored the file byte-identical (after one delete, after an edit, and after all five deleted), and Ctrl+Y + Ctrl+S re-froze it byte-identical. mvn -q compile green, mvn test 345/345, ixd wt done passed. Screenshots tmp/craw35-r01..r08*.png.
